Son tres ecuaciones (cuatro con tres var: These are three equations (four with three variables) in the unknowns $x$, $y$, $λ$. The number $λ$ is the multiplier and measures how much the optimum changes if $c$ changes: $λ = d f^{*}/d c$.
Con la lagrangiana $L = f − λ g$, en cad: With the Lagrangian $L = f − λ g$, at each critical point the Hessian of $L$ is studied only in the directions tangent to the constraint. In two variables, with $t = (−g_y, g_x)$, the sign of $q = t^T H_L t$ decides: $q > 0$ minimum, $q < 0$ maximum (equivalent to the bordered Hessian determinant, with the sign changed). In three variables the Hessian is examined on the tangent plane: two positive eigenvalues, minimum; negative, maximum; mixed, saddle.
